project.title: Black-hole islands as bounded recovery bookkeeping rather than independent Lorentzian transport
project.hidden_assumption: Recovering the Page curve by island formula automatically supplies a microscopic unitary transport mechanism for Hawking radiation.

contradiction.proposition_A: Island formula, replica wormholes, and Hayden-Preskill scrambling solve the black-hole information problem by giving a unitary encoding description.
contradiction.proposition_B: Page-curve recovery and entropic bookkeeping do not by themselves give a microscopic Lorentzian mechanism that transports information into Hawking radiation.
contradiction.why_not_both: A correct entropy curve can be compatible with algebraic recovery while leaving the operational transport channel or boundary algebra choice unresolved.
contradiction.resolution: The reliable result is bounded and low-confidence at the LP level. LP6-S3 gives an L1 boundary-algebra separation proposition: narrow boundary algebra can show an O(1) relative-entropy gap, while wide radiation/bath algebra makes the gap recovery-error controlled. LP6-S1 and Round 1-2 materials strengthen skepticism for flat-space islands, but audits prevent a global no-go theorem.

claims.statement: Island formula can support algebraic recovery/bookkeeping without by itself supplying an independent Lorentzian transport mechanism.

evidence_against: This is L1 conceptual proposition, not an L2 theorem

predictions.statement: In wide-algebra toy models, the relative-entropy gap should scale with approximate recovery error rather than remain O(1).

lessons.lesson: Entropy recovery, algebraic recovery, and microscopic Lorentzian transport must be kept distinct.
A claim with unverified sector-mixing assumptions and strong prior-art overlap must be registered as low-confidence L1, not a theorem.
Negative flat-space-island arguments must explicitly separate project increments from Geng-style operator and factorization arguments.
